subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler: follow-up & proposed POC / next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: John Harper <john.harper@acme.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler — call recap and next steps

Hi John / Sara,

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great overview of ACME's latency guarantees and unpredictable peak traffic windows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our side)
- ACME needs predictable per-request latency for inference (99th percentile SLA target <= 150ms for 8k context).
- Primary workloads: chat assistant (sustained throughput ~120 QPS with bursts to 600 QPS), embeddings for search (batch jobs overnight).
- Key evaluation concerns: provisioning guarantees (reserved capacity vs spot/ephemeral GPU), failover behavior across regions, and cost comparison vs hyperscaler-managed GPU fleet.

How Redwood helps (high level)
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with capacity guarantees, autoscaling policies for burst windows, and SLA options (docs attached).
- Smart routing & fallbacks: route to smaller model variants or cross-region Dedicated pools before falling back to hosted API.
- Cost controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost while hitting latency SLOs.

Proposed short POC (2 weeks)
1) Baseline throughput/latency test vs ACME's typical traffic profile (steady 120 QPS + burst tests up to 600 QPS).
2) Reserved capacity test: provision a Dedicated pool sized to your target 99th percentile SLO; measure steady and burst behavior.
3) Hyperscaler comparison: run the same tests on a configured hyperscaler instance (your team will provide access) and capture tail latency under contention.

Attachments: one-pager comparing Dedicated vs hyperscaler, SLA options, and a Mutual Action Plan spreadsheet — see attached.

Next steps
- Could you confirm the following by end of week so we can schedule the POC?
  1) Who from your infra team will provide hyperscaler test access (they can DM me any temporary creds or a shared endpoint)?
  2) Which dataset/backtest should we use for the chat benchmark?
  3) Preferred POC week (we're available 30 Nov or 7 Dec).

I’ll loop in Camila and Rafael on pricing and procurement once we have the scope.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Hyperscaler_OnePager.pdf, ACME-POC-Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

From: John Harper <john.harper@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler — call recap and next steps

Thanks Markus — that recap is perfect. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Hyperscaler tests: our infra lead Sara (cc'd) can stand up a dedicated cluster in GCP for the bench, but we need an exact instance spec recommendation (GPU type + network egress expectations). Can Redwood advise a comparable hyperscaler config?

2) Capacity guarantees: we care less about single-region failover and more about sustained throughput during unpredictable peaks. If we reserve X v100-equivalent GPUs, will Redwood guarantee that pool will be available for ACME's POCs and production? We may need contractual language for reserved minimums.

3) Cost transparency: please include an estimate for steady-state monthly cost for the Dedicated pool you're proposing, and a line-item comparison to the hyperscaler run-cost (incl. egress + managed infra).

We can aim for the week of 7 Dec for the POC. I'll upload a sample workload trace to the Drive folder you shared.

-John
John Harper
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Corp

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler — pricing/contract language/questions from ACME

Camila / Rafael — forwarding ACME's clarifications. Required asks from them: instance spec guidance for fair hyperscaler comparison, contractual language re reserved minimums, and steady-state vs burst cost estimate.

My take / recommended next moves:
- Instance parity: recommend we propose an equivalent of NVIDIA A100-80GB per slot for hyperscaler baseline; for Dedicated we can size based on effective throughput (we should show tokens/sec and model config). Rafael, can you run a quick back-of-envelope that maps 120 QPS chat workload to N A100-equivalent GPUs and give steady-state and peak reserved counts?

- Reserved guarantees: we can offer Reserved Capacity (monthly commitment) with a contractual SLA for capacity availability during normal maintenance windows; there is an escalation path and compensated credits for missed availability. Camila, can you pull the baseline SLA language (I attached SLA_Options_Redwood.pdf) and flag any clauses that we shouldn't promise to enterprise without legal review?

- Pricing: we should provide (a) committed monthly price for Reserved pool, (b) on-demand burst pricing, and (c) hyperscaler run-cost estimate including egress. I'll draft the high-level comparison after we have Rafael's sizing.

Let’s aim to send ACME a consolidated POC scope + pricing by EOD tomorrow so they can lock the week of 7 Dec.

Thanks — Markus

Markus / Rafael — noted. Rafael, I can take the SLA doc and redact anything that requires Legal review; I'll prepare a short FAQ on what we can commit to for Reserved Capacity vs what goes to Legal for approval.

- Test B: Burst 600 QPS for 10 mins, simultaneous multi-tenant load to measure isolation,

I’ll draft the pricing sheet template with committed vs burst pricing bands. Markus — can you fill in the technical config for the test (model size, seq length, caching behavior)?

- Week of 7 Dec (we provision test infra on Mon 7th, run tests Tues-Wed, analysis Thurs).
- Tech config: model: open-llm-13b quantized profile (8-bit); context length: 8k tokens; baseline payload simulates chat with 120 QPS steady + 600 QPS bursts.
- Hyperscaler parity: A100-80GB equiv for the comparison; ACME to provision GCP instance and share endpoint + temporary account for bench.

What Redwood will deliver
- Dedicated pool with reserved baseline capacity sized to cover steady-state with headroom for a single burst window; autoscale policy enabled for short bursts to handle extra load; logs and per-token latency breakdowns during the test.

- Comparative report (latency percentiles, error rates, cost per 1M tokens) vs hyperscaler setup.

Open items (action owners)
- ACME: provision hyperscaler instance + upload sample trace to Drive (owner: John / Sara) — due 26 Nov.
- Redwood: Rafael to provide sizing & committed pricing, Camila to provide SLA redline and pricing bands — due EOD 19 Nov (Camila / Rafael) — updated: Rafael delivered sizing; Camila providing SLA FAQ by EOD 19 Nov.
